task: Draft a 65–95-word explanation for an upper-elementary history display about these two fictional objects. The class can read dates but is learning why a date on one object cannot automatically date another. Explain what label each object can receive and why the photograph's position on a timeline remains unsettled. The packet descriptions are the only evidence. Do not invent an event identification from the lanterns or retrieve historical images.

facts.text: A printed ticket names the Sunreed Lantern Fair and bears the date March 14, 1932.
A separate photograph shows a crowd carrying lanterns; it has no caption or date.
Nothing in the packet links the photograph to the fair named on the ticket.
The ticket can be labeled with its printed event and date; the photograph's event and date remain unknown.

forbidden_additions: A claim that the photograph shows the Sunreed Lantern Fair
An invented photograph date or definite order between the two objects
A claim of image retrieval or external historical verification
preserve: The photograph's date and event are not established
An explanation based on source relationships rather than assumed learner competence
